title: Computer Science Algorithms & TOC Targeted Quiz

questions.question_text: Consider a complete bipartite graph K_{m, n}. What is the number of edges and the condition under which K_{m, n} contains an Eulerian circuit?
questions.option_a: m*n edges; Eulerian circuit exists if and only if both m and n are even.
questions.option_b: m+n edges; Eulerian circuit exists if and only if both m and n are odd.
questions.option_c: m*n edges; Eulerian circuit exists if and only if m = n.
questions.option_d: (m*n)/2 edges; Eulerian circuit exists if and only if m is even.
questions.explanation: In K_{m, n}, every vertex in the first partition of size m has degree n, and every vertex in the second partition of size n has degree m. A connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if EVERY vertex has an even degree. Thus, both m (degree of n vertices) and n (degree of m vertices) must be even.
questions.numerical_formula: Eulerian Graph Condition: deg(v) mod 2 == 0 for all v in V. Edges in K_{m, n} = m * n.
questions.common_pitfalls: Confusing Eulerian path (which allows exactly two odd-degree vertices) with Eulerian circuit (requires all even).

questions.question_text: Which of the following problems is DECIDABLE for Context-Free Languages (CFLs)?
questions.option_d: Intersection emptiness (Is L1 intersection L2 = empty?)
questions.explanation: For Context-Free Languages: (1) Membership (w in L): Decidable via CYK algorithm O(n^3). (2) Emptiness (L = empty): Decidable by checking if the start symbol can derive any terminal string. (3) Finiteness: Decidable via cycle detection in reduced CFG. In contrast, Universality, Equivalence, and Intersection-Emptiness are UNDECIDABLE for CFLs.
questions.numerical_formula: Decidability Chart for CFL: Membership (D), Emptiness (D), Finiteness (D), Equivalence (U), Subset (U), Disjointness (U), Universality (U).
questions.common_pitfalls: Assuming that because Equivalence is decidable for Regular languages, it is also decidable for CFLs.

questions.question_text: In heuristic search, an A* search algorithm is guaranteed to return an optimal solution path (admissible) on tree search if the heuristic function h(n) satisfies which condition?
questions.option_a: h(n) <= h*(n) for all nodes n (Underestimation of true cost to goal)
questions.option_b: h(n) >= h*(n) for all nodes n (Overestimation of true cost to goal)
questions.option_d: h(n) is monotonic and strictly decreasing along every path
questions.explanation: An admissible heuristic never overestimates the true remaining cost to reach the goal: 0 <= h(n) <= h*(n) for all nodes n. For graph search, consistency (monotonicity: h(n) <= c(n, a, n') + h(n')) is additionally required to ensure optimal paths without node re-opening.
questions.numerical_formula: A* Evaluation Function: f(n) = g(n) + h(n). Admissibility: h(n) <= h*(n). Consistency: h(A) <= c(A, B) + h(B).
questions.common_pitfalls: Remember: Overestimating breaks optimality because A* may terminate prematurely on a suboptimal goal.
